Advances: ancora.findings

Base moved by orchestrator ruling 2026-09-03T23:55Z: the stage fast-forwards onto epic tip 846e942 (gg8.2's governance rule is live there), so spec.check runs with --base 846e942 and no change/missing_decision trailer is needed.

Wave 1 of ancora-gg8 (C2 in the investigation record; findings-C and the architecture decision are comments there). Root cause: overrides match (subject, code) only because the Finding struct drops the requirement id its creation sites already pass. Atlas had to mute tags/new_requirement_untagged across a 34-requirement subject to acknowledge one blocked requirement, with an apology in the reason field.

Deliverable:
An optional `requirement:` key on `.spec/config.yml` override entries that narrows the match to one requirement id. Five contained edits, fully backward compatible:
1. Finding: keep the optional :requirement field on the struct (lib/ancora/finding.ex:11-18, 135-142) — creation sites already pass it (lib/ancora/verifier.ex:144, lib/ancora/tag_findings.ex:100, 157).
2. Severity.resolve_finding: put finding.requirement into opts (lib/ancora/severity.ex:143-148).
3. Config.Override: optional requirement field; matching becomes today's check plus `ovr.requirement in [nil, finding_requirement]` (lib/ancora/config.ex:32-42, 163-167). An entry without requirement: behaves exactly as today.
4. parse_override_entry: accept optional requirement, validate against known claim ids the way subject validates against known_subjects (lib/ancora/config.ex:392-465); unknown id produces config/invalid_value and the entry is ignored.
5. Config moduledoc + scaffold docs mention the key. Any override may carry requirement:; it simply never matches findings that have no requirement (no per-code validation — declined on the epic).
subject_status/2 continues to label a subject acknowledged when any override names it, requirement-scoped included.

Spec delta (land in this same diff):
Edit the `ancora.findings.per_subject_overrides` statement: entries carry subject, code, severity, required reason, "and an optional `requirement:` that narrows the override to findings attributed to that requirement id; an entry without it applies subject-wide as before. An entry naming an unknown requirement id shall produce `config/invalid_value` and be ignored." Add scenario `ancora.findings.scenario.override_scoped_to_requirement` — given two requirements R1 and R2 of subject A both firing tags/requirement_untagged and an override for subject A, that code, `requirement: R1`, severity info, when severities resolve, then R1's finding is info with severity_source :config and R2's stays at its default.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests for the new scenario; existing config/severity/override suites; a parse test for the unknown-requirement entry.
- Behaviors to demonstrate: override_scoped_to_requirement; existing override_scoped_to_subject unchanged; entry without requirement: byte-identical behavior to today.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: no new callable surface; the widened Override flows through the existing Severity.resolve_all path (lib/ancora/gate.ex:351).

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/gate.ex EXCEPT validate_override_subjects/2 (extend it to validate override requirement ids; orchestrator ruling 2026-09-04T00:05Z after audit bounce 1)
- lib/ancora/derive/**
- lib/ancora/output*.ex
- lib/ancora/trailer.ex

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/finding.ex
- lib/ancora/severity.ex
- lib/ancora/config.ex
- test/**
- lib/ancora/status.ex (status.ex:28 known_requirements mirror; ruling 2026-09-04T00:05Z)
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (validate_override_subjects/2 requirement mirror only; ruling 2026-09-04T00:05Z)
- priv/spec_init/config.yml.eex (scaffold template comment documenting the optional `requirement:` key; added by orchestrator ruling 2026-09-03T22:52Z because deliverable item 5 names the scaffold docs)
- .spec/specs/ancora.findings.spec.md (the statement edit and scenario above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)
- .spec/specs/ancora.scaffold.spec.md (one substantive sentence: the scaffold config template documents the optional `requirement:` override key; orchestrator ruling 2026-09-03T23:55Z)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No trailer grammar changes (requirement scoping is config-only; the trailer stays code-keyed per the sfu ruling)
- No restriction on which codes accept requirement: (declined on the epic)
- No changes to how subject_status labels acknowledged subjects

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

Mutation: change `ovr.requirement in [nil, requirement]` (lib/ancora/config.ex:178) to `ovr.requirement == requirement`. Result: full suite green (349 tests, same 2 env failures as baseline). Production findings carry requirement ids (lib/ancora/verifier.ex:144, lib/ancora/tag_findings.ex:100), so that mutation silently disables every existing subject-wide override on tags/* findings. This is the ticket's "entry without requirement: byte-identical to today" behaviour and it is unproven. Fix: in "an override applies only to the named subject" (or a new test) give finding `a` a `requirement: "subject.a.r1"` and assert it still resolves info/:config; the existing `subject_only` finding at :281 covers the opposite direction (scoped override, requirement-less finding) but not this one.

No production caller does (lib/ancora.ex:36, lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex:22, lib/ancora/status.ex:28, lib/ancora/project_info.ex:155), and gate.ex:202 validate_override_subjects checks subjects only. So the spec sentence tagged here ("An entry naming an unknown requirement id shall produce config/invalid_value and be ignored") is proven only for a call shape the gate never uses; in a real run an unknown id is silently accepted. gate.ex is out of this ticket's scope, so this needs a ruling: either wire known_requirements (gate post-index, like subjects) or soften the spec sentence to "when the requirement corpus is supplied".

The fixture sets override severity `info`, and tags/requirement_untagged's registry default is also `info` (lib/ancora/finding.ex:56). `r2.severity == :info` and `subject_only.severity == :info` stay green under mutation 1 (drop the requirement check) and mutation 5 (discard the parsed requirement); only the severity_source assertions catch them. Reasoning: I re-derived both verifier Gaps by reading, not running, and both hold. So the new spec sentence "An entry naming an unknown ... requirement id ... shall produce config/invalid_value and be ignored" is false on every shipped path; the only proving test (test/ancora/config_test.exs:303) supplies the option itself. This is NOT parity with the subject check: the gate validates unknown subjects today (gate.ex:202) and status does at load (status.ex:28); only the `validate` path (ancora.ex:36) skips both. Gap 2: the mutation `ovr.requirement in [nil, requirement]` -> `== requirement` (config.ex:178) survives by inspection. Every subject-wide-override test pairs a nil-requirement override with a nil-requirement finding (config_test.exs:222-252 uses derived/unanchored_subject with no requirement; gate_test.exs:472 same code; severity_test.exs has zero Finding.new calls with requirement:), and the new test's requirement-less finding (config_test.exs:281) is checked against a requirement-SCOPED override. Production findings on tags/requirement_untagged and spec/requirement_unverified always carry a requirement id (tag_findings.ex:100, verifier.ex:144), so the mutation would silently disable Atlas's actual subject-wide override and ship green. Both Gaps are already named by the verifier, so this routes to the implementer. Land in one pass:

1. Wire status.ex (authorized by orchestrator ruling; status.ex is not in Out-of-Scope). At lib/ancora/status.ex:27-28 replace the Config.load call with:
   requirement_ids =
     Enum.flat_map(index["subjects"], fn subject ->
       subject["requirements"] |> List.wrap() |> Enum.map(& &1["id"]) |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
     end)
   config = Config.load(root, known_subjects: subject_ids, known_requirements: requirement_ids)
   (index subjects carry a string-keyed "requirements" list of maps with "id"; parser.ex:54/102, same shape tag_findings.ex:93-95 reads via id_of.)
